What we do

Four sweet reasons to push open the door.

Toby and Peggy Wenham opened this shop in 2005 inside the original Enumclaw National Bank building, scooping local Snoqualmie ice cream and making candy from Peggy's mother's recipes. Today the Harris family keeps every bit of it going — same building, same scoops, same wall of tea.

Snoqualmie ice cream

Scooped from a local Washington creamery — Cascade Blackberry to Kahlua Almond Fudge, with dairy-free flavors always in the case.

Homemade candy

Fudge, caramels and peanut brittle made in-house the old way — including a habanero caramel with a real kick.

The tea wall

A hundred-plus jars of loose leaf: Purple Mountain Majesty, Sunset in Seattle, Cream Earl Grey, Masala Chai and friends.

Espresso & more

Espresso drinks, hand-dipped chocolates, freeze-dried candy, scone mixes and jams — the awning wasn't kidding.

Our story

A bank that started holding better things.

The building at 1215 Griffin Avenue was the original Enumclaw National Bank. Since 2005, its vault-solid walls have held fudge, caramels, a hundred teas, and roughly twenty-six tubs of ice cream a week.

From Almost to Sweet.

Toby and Peggy Wenham had run Almost Necessities, their gift and craft shop, since 1994. When the space next door opened up in 2005, they didn't lease it to an office — they filled it with candy. The fudge, caramels and peanut brittle came from recipes handed down from Peggy's mother and her high-school home-economics classes, and the ice cream came from Snoqualmie Gourmet, a creamery just up the road.

Enumclaw noticed. So did everyone else: in 2019, Insider named Sweet Necessities the best ice cream shop in the entire state of Washington.

When the Wenhams retired, the shop passed to the Harris family, who run it today — same building, same recipes' spirit, same line out the door on a warm Saturday.

🏆 Insider's best ice cream shop in Washington state, 2019
